$comment: D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET -- the RUN witness for a C23 6.2.2 OBJECT-IDENTITY property, and the reason it needs TWO IMAGES. ★★★ THE GENERAL RULE: AN OBJECT-IDENTITY PROPERTY CANNOT BE WITNESSED BY ONE IMAGE. A test asserting that a symbol denotes the SAME OBJECT throughout the program MUST involve a SECOND image DSS did not build -- so this example dlopens a gcc-built `.so` that is SHIPPED PREBUILT beside it (one per ELF arch: libdss_env_probe_x86_64.so, libdss_env_probe_aarch64.so, source env_probe_so.c, build command recorded in that file) and every identity assertion crosses that image boundary. Prebuilt on purpose: the example needs NO host cross-compiler at test time, and both runners mirror the example dir's whole file neighborhood into the run cwd, so `./libdss_env_probe_<arch>.so` resolves. THE DEFECT: DSS used to bind an ET_EXEC's imported library DATA objects by ELF COPY RELOCATION (a `.bss` slot + a DEFINED OBJECT dynsym + one R_*_COPY; ld.so memcpy's the library's object in). A copy relocation redirects the library's references FOR THE ONE NAME THE EXEC CLAIMS, and ✔MEASURED, glibc exports ONE environment object under THREE names -- `__environ` GLOBAL, `_environ` and `environ` WEAK, all at 0x20ad58 (x86_64) / 0x1b7288 (aarch64). DSS's descriptor names `__environ`, so `__libc_start_main` wrote envp into the exec's copy while libc's own `environ` slot was NEVER written: a third-party libtcl8.6.so reading the un-prefixed `environ` saw NULL and SIGSEGV'd in TclSetupEnv+0xe8 (regression pair `09e1608a` green -> `6f4aab73` rc=139), with no diagnostic anywhere and a binary that looked perfect under readelf. C23 6.2.2 requires an identifier with external linkage to denote THE SAME OBJECT throughout the program; `environ` itself is POSIX, so the conformance surface is OBJECT IDENTITY, not the symbol. THE FIX BEING WITNESSED: every ELF format now declares dataImportBinding:got-indirect, the exec DEFINES NOTHING (its data imports stay UNDEF/st_size 0 and take a GOT slot + R_*_GLOB_DAT), and the copy-relocation mechanism is DELETED from the vocabulary rather than left inert. ★ got-indirect IS legal in a non-PIE ET_EXEC: a non-PIE exec has a .got and R_*_GLOB_DAT rows in .rela.dyn are load-time work ld.so does with no PIE requirement -- ✔MEASURED, these very binaries. ★ WHY THE PREDECESSOR WITNESS (examples/c-subset/shipped_environ) COULD NOT SEE IT: it read `environ` through the DSS macro and cross-checked with libc's own `getenv`, but BOTH reads went through the very name the exec claimed, so it compared the exec's copy WITH ITSELF -- a SELF-LOOP, structurally unable to fail, born vacuous, green on all four legs across the entire regression window. WHAT THIS PROGRAM ASSERTS, five things, exit codes in main.c: (a) ★ THE WITNESS IS VERIFIED BEFORE THE SUBJECT IS -- main.c PARSES the shipped .so's own dynamic relocations (Elf64_Rela r_info>>32 -> .dynsym -> the NUL-terminated string at .dynstr+st_name) and requires >=1 naming exactly `environ` and ZERO naming `__environ`; a .so that happened to reference the PREFIXED spelling would make everything else vacuous in exactly the way the old witness was. ⚠ TWO measured traps that a naive check falls into: `ld` points `environ`'s st_name INTO THE MIDDLE of `dss_probe_environ_object` (tail-suffix string sharing), so scanning .dynstr for a standalone "environ" reports a FALSE PRESENT; and readelf prints `environ@GLIBC_2.2.5` while the RAW st_name is exactly `environ` (the version suffix is synthesized from .gnu.version). (b) A VALUE, never mere survival: the library reports how many entries IT sees and the VALUE it finds for the variable this image's environ[0] names, and they must be byte-identical -- the library walks `environ` ITSELF, deliberately NOT getenv, which reads libc's internal `__environ` and would keep agreeing with a copy while the un-prefixed object stayed empty. (c) ★ THE `if (environ)` ARM gets its own exit code (30): a library that merely TESTS the pointer sees NULL, takes a wrong branch and NEVER CRASHES -- the silent half of the defect. (d) ★ THE MATCHED gcc-REFERENCE CONTROL, same runner and same PROCESS: `&environ` as gcc-compiled code binds it must equal `&environ` as DSS-compiled code binds it. Two independent compilers agreeing on ONE address is what makes a future divergence ATTRIBUTABLE rather than argued. (e) ★ SAME_OBJECT=YES, the diagnosis instrument promoted to a shipped assertion: dlsym of BOTH spellings must return the SAME non-null address, and it must be the address both compilers bound. ★ THE HANDLE MUST BE THE GLOBAL ONE (dlopen(NULL,...)) -- ✔MEASURED the hard way: dlsym on a SPECIFIC library handle searches that library and its dependencies only, reaching libc's ORIGINAL storage and skipping the executable, and asked that way a matched `gcc -no-pie` control FAILS TOO (gcc copy-relocates into its own .bss, so the exec's definition is the live object). A check a correct reference compiler fails is a broken check, not a finding. BOTH ELF ARCHES, and not for symmetry: the bug was arm64-VISIBLE and x86_64-LATENT, so a single-arch witness would have missed this one and will miss the next. ✔MEASURED GREEN: DSS x86_64 rc=42, DSS aarch64 under qemu-aarch64 rc=42, and a matched `gcc -std=gnu17 -no-pie -D_GNU_SOURCE` build of THIS SAME main.c rc=42 with byte-identical stdout. RED-ON-DISABLE, each MEASURED, none a line-count check: (1) rebuild the shipped .so against the PREFIXED `__environ` -> exit 13, the witness refuses to certify itself; (2) delete the shipped .so -> exit 10, never a skip; (3) reproduce the historical split shape with gcc (a -no-pie exec that copy-relocates ONLY `__environ`) beside the good .so -> exit 30, i.e. the library sees environ==NULL with NO crash, which is precisely the state the old witness reported as green; (4) declare dataImportBinding:"copy-relocation" on any format -> REFUSED AT LOAD by the closed-enum check naming the file, because the value was deleted from the vocabulary. elf-ONLY on purpose: ✔MEASURED, no Windows CRT exports a spelling ucrtbase can bind (ucrtbase: none of the three; msvcrt: only the underscored `_environ`) and the macho export is unmeasured, so both stay honest S0001 per this directory's need-driven staging rule. exec-only for the same reason as its stdio sibling: the pie/dyn flavours are a different image shape, and this defect was the EXEC arm's.
